items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joey Jones was on trumpet and I was on bass

ctx.x: I stayed… we went to the….as I said in traveling down South, things got a little bad because they didn‟t like us coming down with all those beautiful shows, Gal Of Mine, and great dancers, comedians and things. So that stopped, got cut out, and finances got small. So we come down to seven pieces where we could do small clubs in towns like Seattle, San Francisco, Chicago. Went down to seven pieces; Sam The Man Taylor, Panama Francis had come in the band then, Kay Johnson, trombone was still there, David Rivera was…

The first time I ever played with you I filled in for Dave. Dave was a neighbor of mine. We live in Riverton and he was a neighbor of mine and I don‟t know, somebody, I guess his wife… something happened suddenly and he called me, he said, “Look, bail me out. I can‟t do”… whatever it was, and I went down and played the show. It‟s the first time I played with you. Man, it‟s like riding in a Rolls Royce, I said all right
